subject: general
question: Which of the following solutions may scatter light?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Colloidal** **solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Light scatters** in a variety of directions through a colloidal solution.
 
• As a result of the **Tyndall effect**.
 
• The** Tyndall** effect is a phenomenon that occurs when particles in a colloidal solution **scatter light**.
 
• The light frequency and particle density both affect how much scattering occurs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **colloidal** particles in the solution prevent a **light beam **from passing completely through a colloid when it does so.
 
• The light is **scattered** when it strikes the colloidal **particles**. 
 
• The **Tyndall **Effect is a light scattering phenomenon that only occurs in colloidal **dispersion** and does not exist in a true solution.
 
• This result is used to distinguish between a true **solution** and a colloid in a **mixture**.
